Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

thermify (development version)

Changes

  • The automatic installation of the tempify Python backend is now opt-in: thermify never downloads Python or tempify unless the user asks for it, with install_tempify() or with options(thermify.tempify_auto = TRUE) (or THERMIFY_TEMPIFY_AUTO=true) before loading the package. Before, it was on by default in interactive sessions. A Python chosen by the user and an existing install_tempify() environment are used as before, and without tempify all computations use the equivalent native R engine. The error raised when the tempify engine is requested but unavailable now says how to install it.
  • When temporal = "auto" (or engine = "auto") falls back to the native engine because tempify is not installed, a note says, once per session, that tempify is optional and how to install it. It is not shown during package checks, and options(thermify.tempify_hint = FALSE) hides it.

thermify 0.5.0

First release validated against observed hourly temperatures (30 CEAZA-Met stations), with a change of default that follows from that validation, and WorldClim CMIP6 projections. Results of thermify() and thermify_rast() change only for chilling hours when ch_methods is not set (see “Breaking changes”); all other methods and indices are unchanged. Archived on Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24407244.

The validation covers the semi-arid north-central Chile (Coquimbo and Atacama regions, from the coast to 2,543 m). It has not yet been repeated in the central-south: hourly records were requested from INIA, and the recommendations may need revision for wetter or colder climates.

Not yet included: the Winkler, Huglin and Cool Night viticultural indices.

Breaking changes

  • thermify() and thermify_rast() now count chilling hours on the hourly temperatures by default (ch_methods = "hourly", from observed or reconstructed hourly series) instead of the analytical sine estimate from daily extremes ("sine"). In the CEAZA-Met validation the hourly count (Linvill reconstruction) was within 1 % of the observed chilling hours, against -9 % for the sine estimate. Results keyed ch_sine are now ch_hourly; set ch_methods = "sine" to keep the previous output. A note is shown once per session when the default is used (#43).

New features

  • worldclim_future_region() reads WorldClim 2.1 downscaled CMIP6 projections (monthly tmin, tmax, prec at 30 arc-seconds) for a region, reading only the bytes of the region from the global files (about 5 GB each) and caching the result. worldclim_cmip6_gcms lists the available global climate models.

Changes

  • validate_station() also evaluates degree-days computed on the hourly reconstructions from daily extremes ("hourly_linvill", "hourly_sine"), at the daily, monthly and gridded levels.

Documentation

  • New article “Projected change of thermal indices: WorldClim CMIP6”: change of degree-days, chilling hours, Utah units and chill portions by 2041-2060 (14 GCMs, SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5) over the province of Cauquenes, and at 29 CEAZA-Met stations with a delta method applied to the observed hourly records. Scripts in data-raw/climate-change/.
  • New article “Validation with observed hourly temperature: CEAZA-Met network” with the results of the 30-station validation, per-station figures and practical guidance; vignette("validation") summarises them.
  • vignette("gdd-methods") (“Which method?”) and the synthetic comparison article are updated: the observed stations contradict the synthetic ranking of degree-day methods in semi-arid climates.

Validation

  • First empirical validation with observed hourly temperature: 30 stations of the CEAZA-Met network (Coquimbo and Atacama regions), with scripts in data-raw/validation-ceaza/. Only derived seasonal totals and metrics are stored in the repository; the hourly records stay with CEAZA.

thermify 0.4.0

Adds the modified average degree-day method and experimental ensembles of degree-day methods, and documents a controlled comparison of all methods on synthetic temperatures. Results of the existing methods are unchanged. Archived on Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24385014.

Not yet included: validation against observed hourly station records (data requested from CEAZA and INIA, issue #3), and the Winkler and Huglin viticultural indices.

New features

  • degree_days() gains method = "modified_average" (McMaster & Wilhelm 1997, method 2): the daily extremes are bounded by the base and upper thresholds before averaging, as in the “86/50” rule for maize. It is also available in thermify(), thermify_rast() and validate_station() through gdd_methods.
  • GDD ensembles (experimental): gdd_ensemble_weights() estimates the weights of a combination of daily GDD methods from validate_station() results with observed hourly data, by stacking (default), Bayesian model averaging or Akaike weights, and assesses it by leave-one-station-out cross-validation. degree_days(method = "ensemble"), gdd_ensemble() (weighted mean plus the spread between members) and gdd_methods = "ensemble" with gdd_weights in thermify() and thermify_rast() apply the weights. No default weights are shipped: they depend on the climate, the base temperature and the data available.

Documentation

  • New article “Degree-day methods compared on synthetic temperatures”: a controlled experiment with synthetic daily and hourly temperatures generated from WorldClim normals at four sites in the Maule Region (Parton & Logan diurnal model), comparing every GDD method at the daily, monthly and climatological levels. Reproducible with data-raw/gdd-synthetic/run.R. It complements, and does not replace, validation against observed station data. Its figures show the bias of each method by level of information and site, and the seasonal bias next to the monthly reference degree-days.
  • README with an animated demo, a one-line summary, the install command and a link to the live Cauquenes example; social preview image (man/figures/social-preview.png), rebuilt with data-raw/readme-figures.R.
  • Contributing guide, Contributor Covenant code of conduct, issue forms (bug report, feature request) and a pull request template.

thermify 0.3.1

Prepares the package for a CRAN submission: no Python is downloaded during package checks or in non-interactive sessions, and the package metadata cite the methods with DOIs. Results are unchanged. Archived on Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23937033.

Changes

  • The automatic tempify set-up now runs only in interactive sessions and never while a package is being checked; in scripts, enable it with THERMIFY_TEMPIFY_AUTO=true. A Python chosen by the user and the "r-thermify" environment of install_tempify() are always used.
  • tempify_available() no longer starts Python when none is configured, so recent versions of ‘reticulate’ do not download one to answer it.

Documentation

  • DESCRIPTION cites the methods with DOIs and includes the maintainer’s ORCID; Language: en-GB and a word list for spell checks.
  • Network examples write to tempdir(); cran-comments.md documents the network and Python behaviour for a CRAN submission.

thermify 0.3.0

Adds plot() and print() methods for raster results, sets up the tempify backend automatically, and turns the Cauquenes tutorial into a worked example with computed results for the whole province. Archived on Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23922611.

Breaking changes

  • thermify_rast() returns an object of class "thermify_rast" instead of a plain list. It is still a named list of SpatRaster, so x$cp_dynamic, names(x) and lapply(x, ...) work as before; only code that tests the class exactly (for example identical(class(x), "list")) is affected.

New features

  • thermify_rast() returns an object of class "thermify_rast" (still a named list of SpatRaster) with a plot() method: variable selects indices or families, type the layer ("season", "annual", "monthly" or months such as "m07"), nrow/ncol the layout, plus col, boundary, a common or per-panel colour scale and titles; and a print() method that summarises indices, units, layers and files. Titles that do not fit in a panel are wrapped onto several lines; a single index shown month by month gets short titles (month and units) with the index name above the panels; months without data (outside the chill period) are left out. Default palettes are multi-hue sequential (YlOrRd, YlGnBu, BuPu, YlGn), Utah units crossing zero use a diverging palette centred on zero, and col accepts any hcl.colors() palette name such as "Spectral".
  • tempify is set up automatically. With reticulate (>= 1.41) thermify declares it with reticulate::py_require() on load, and the first use of the tempify engine builds and caches a Python environment with it. install_tempify() creates a persistent environment "r-thermify" instead, which is then used on load. A Python chosen by the user is respected; options(thermify.tempify_auto = FALSE) or THERMIFY_TEMPIFY_AUTO=false disables the setup.
  • tempify_version() records the tempify git commit also when tempify was installed from a git URL (PEP 610 direct_url.json).

Documentation

  • vignette("cauquenes") is evaluated when the documentation site is built and shows results for the whole province of Cauquenes (4,554 WorldClim 2.1 cells at 30 arc-seconds): climatology, seasonal indices for the town, maps drawn with plot(), the annual cycle month by month, spatial statistics and method differences. Package checks still show the code only, with a link to the site.
  • vignette("tempify-integration") explains how tempify is installed.

thermify 0.2.0

Adds the tools for empirical validation against station records, the official DPA 2023 boundaries of Cauquenes, and attaches terra with the package. Validation results with real stations (#3) are not part of this release. Archived on Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23905378.

Breaking changes

  • terra is now a dependency (Depends) instead of a suggested package: installing thermify installs terra, and library(thermify) attaches it, so vect(), rast(), plot() and the other terra functions are available without terra::. On Linux, terra needs the GDAL, GEOS and PROJ system libraries.

New features

  • cauquenes dataset: official DPA 2023 boundaries of the Cauquenes commune and province (packed SpatVector, EPSG:5360), replacing the undocumented cauquenes.gpkg referenced in earlier documentation.
  • cauquenes_boundary() returns one or both levels as a SpatVector, optionally projected (crs).
  • Station validation (#3): prepare_station_hourly() regularises hourly records, fills short gaps and flags incomplete days; validate_station() compares indices observed on hourly data with estimates from daily extremes, from the station’s densified monthly climatology and, optionally, from a gridded climatology; validation_metrics() returns bias, MAE, RMSE, relative bias and correlation. The protocol is tested on synthetic records; results with real stations are pending.

Documentation

  • The cauquenes dataset cites its source (SUBDERE, DPA 2023) and carries the DIFROL circulation notice (Resolución Nº 87 de 2023).
  • vignette("validation") documents the implementation; examples, the Cauquenes tutorial and the README use cauquenes_boundary() and bare terra calls.
  • Release and development version badges in the README and the site.

thermify 0.1.0

Archived on Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23841857.

First release. Functional, documented and tested package for agroclimatic thermal indices: growing degree-days, chilling hours, Utah chill units and Dynamic model chill portions, from hourly, daily or monthly temperatures, for single sites and rasters.

Verified on Ubuntu (R release and oldrel), Windows and macOS. Results based on monthly climatologies are model-based estimates; empirical validation against station data is planned (see vignette("validation")).

Breaking changes

  • degree_days() gains method as its third argument and defaults to "single_sine". The previous behaviour (daily average) is method = "average". Name base explicitly in existing calls.
  • chill_hours() gains method as its third argument; lower and upper must now be named when passed by position.

New features

  • Growing degree-days by the average, single/double sine and single/double triangle methods, with horizontal, vertical and intermediate upper cutoffs (degree_days()), and degree-hours (degree_hours()).
  • Chilling hours from daily extremes (analytical sine and triangle, numerical reference) and counted on hourly data (chill_hours_hourly()).
  • Utah model chill units (chill_units(), utah_weights()).
  • Dynamic model chill portions with state carried across blocks (chill_portions()).
  • Hourly reconstruction with the Linvill and continuous sine models (hourly_temperatures(), daylength()).
  • Monthly-to-daily densification through tempify or a native pchip_mp engine, with consistency checks and diagnostics (densify_monthly(), densify_diagnostics(), tempify_available(), tempify_version()).
  • Accumulation periods that may cross the year end (season_days()).
  • threshold_date() returns the date on which an accumulated index reaches a requirement (for example a degree-day or chill-portion target).
  • Progress reporting (blocks, percentage, elapsed time, ETA) in thermify_rast() and for archive downloads, controlled by progress or the option thermify.progress.
  • Integrated workflows for one site (thermify()) and for monthly SpatRaster stacks processed in blocks (thermify_rast()), with GeoTIFF, NetCDF and provenance output.
  • WorldClim 2.1 helpers: worldclim_region() reads 30 arc-second normals for a region (extent or polygon, optional mask) through HTTP range requests on the remote tiles, without downloading global or country files; worldclim_monthly(), study_window(), check_monthly_climate().
  • Cauquenes case study in examples/cauquenes.

Verification

  • Cross-checks against chillR and degday in inst/verification/verify_references.R.

Documentation

  • User stories with acceptance tests (docs/USER_STORIES.md, tests/testthat/test-story-*.R) and a testing strategy (docs/TESTING.md): unit, acceptance, integration and error-path tests, 397 expectations and 94 % line coverage with all optional groups.
